name: Prompt: A Journal of Academic Writing Assignments
content_scope: Peer-reviewed writing assignments across the disciplines, each published as a reflective essay plus the assignment sheet (often with rubrics and supplements as separate galleys). Vol. 1 (2017) through Vol. 10 No. 2 (2026): 19 issues, 110 assignment articles plus editors' notes. Special issues on social justice (2021, 2022), law school transition (2024), NYU writing programs (2025), and the Southwest (2026).
default_license: CC BY-NC 4.0
api_notes: OJS 3.3.0.21. OAI-PMH endpoint verified: https://thepromptjournal.com/index.php/prompt/oai (Identify returns repositoryName and protocol 2.0; earliest datestamp 2020-10-25). Article landing pages carry DC/citation_* meta tags (abstract, DOI 10.31719/pjaw.*, pdf URLs). Issue archive at /issue/archive (single page). Atom feed linked in page head.
notes: Every article page shows a CC BY-NC 4.0 badge; the journal's Open Access Policy also specifies CC BY-NC. Authors retain copyright. Mirrored/listed at https://wacclearinghouse.org/prompt/. Full assignment-level catalog is in assignments_other.json (ids prefixed 'prompt-').

name: CORA (Community of Online Research Assignments)
content_scope: Librarian- and faculty-contributed information literacy lesson plans, assignments, and teaching resources, tagged by discipline, ACRL frame, tags, and ability level, with downloadable attachments.
default_license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 US
item_count_estimate: 147 lessons listed under English, Multidisciplinary, Business, and Education discipline pages (Oct 2026); site-wide total not stated
api_notes: Main /search page is behind a Cloudflare Turnstile challenge (do not automate). Discipline listing pages are plain HTML and paginate with ?page=N, e.g. /discipline/english (4 pages), /discipline/multidisciplinary (10 pages), /discipline/writing, /discipline/business, /discipline/education. Lesson pages expose title, 'Submitted by', posted date, suggested citation, disciplines, tags, ability level, license link, and attachment URLs under /sites/default/files/attachments/. RSS at https://projectcora.org/rss.xml carries only the 5 newest items.
notes: Every lesson page sampled (147) displays 'This content is available under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 United States license.' 74 writing-relevant lessons catalogued (ids prefixed 'cora-'). Footer links a Terms of Use page.

name: ACRL Framework for Information Literacy Sandbox
content_scope: Lesson plans, activities, assignment prompts, rubrics, syllabi, and other materials tied to the ACRL Framework, filterable by discipline (including 'Rhetoric, Composition, and Writing'), frame, resource type, scope, institution type, and license.
default_license: Varies by item (contributor picks All Rights Reserved or a CC license)
api_notes: Drupal views with GET filters: /resources?field_discipline_term=81 (Rhetoric, Composition, and Writing), 42 (English); field_resource_type_term=15040 (Assignment Prompt), 15055 (Syllabus), 15039 (Lesson Plan), 76 (Activity), 66 (Rubric), 15042 (Worksheet); field_license takes a string such as 'All Rights Reserved'; pagination ?page=N. Item pages list contributor, description, resource types, frames, disciplines, 'License Assigned', and file links under /system/files?file=...
notes: Many items are 'All Rights Reserved' (e.g., The Metaliterati Project TTRPG); check the License Assigned field per item. Footer links ALA copyright statement. Items catalogued with ids prefixed 'acrl-'.

name: Writing Spaces Assignments and Activities Archive
content_scope: Assignments and activities curated as an open companion to the Writing Spaces readings series, organized in 16 topic categories (Rhetorical & Genre Awareness, Research, Language & Power, Artificial Intelligence, Multimodal Composition, Technical and Professional Writing, etc.), each split into Assignments and Activities.
default_license: Not stated on archive index (footer: 'Copyright © 2026 Writing Spaces'); Writing Spaces volumes are CC-licensed
api_notes: WordPress site; item URLs follow /writingspaces/[slug]/. writingspaces.org links the archive from its navigation; writingspaces.org/assignments-activities-archive/ returned HTTP 500 on 17 Oct 2026.
notes: Repository record only; item-level cataloguing is handled by another agent. Items are described as reviewed by the Writing Spaces editorial team. Check each item page for its own license.

name: TextGenEd: Teaching with Text Generation Technologies (and TextGenEd: Continuing Experiments)
content_scope: Peer/editorially reviewed undergraduate assignments that use or critique text generation and generative AI, grouped as AI Literacy, Creative Explorations, Ethical Considerations, Professional Writing, Rhetorical Engagements, and (from 2024) Prompt Engineering. Original collection Aug 2023 (34 assignments) plus annual 'Continuing Experiments' releases (Jan 2024: 16; Aug 2024: 15; Aug 2025: 23; Aug 2026: 15).
default_license: CC BY-NC (version not specified)
api_notes: WordPress/Elementor pages under /repository/collections/textgened/<section>/<slug>/ and /repository/collections/continuing-experiments/<release>/<section>/<slug>/. Pages include Learning Goals, Original Assignment Context, Materials Needed, Time Frame, Overview, and assignment text; DOIs 10.37514/TWR-J.2023.2982.2.xx for the 2023 set.
notes: Editors Annette Vee, Tim Laquintano, Carly Schnitzler. License language: intro to the 2023 collection says 'all of the assignments are licensed as Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial'; Continuing Experiments intro says 'each assignment is licensed CC-BY-NC' and release pages carry a 'CC Notice' (CC-BY-NC). Individual assignment pages show only the site-wide copyright footer. Catalogued with ids prefixed 'textgened-'.

name: WAC Clearinghouse: The WAC Repository
content_scope: Peer-reviewed articles and books on WAC plus curated and crowdsourced collections, exhibits, statements, and teaching resources (collections include TextGenEd, TextGenEd: Continuing Experiments, Grant Abstracts, and AI Text Generators and Teaching Writing).
default_license: Varies; site footer: copyright held by authors and editors
api_notes: Collections index at /repository/collections/. The Clearinghouse also hosts open books (many CC BY-NC-ND) and more than two dozen OA journals; the older 'teaching exchange' pages were not found at /resources/ (404).
notes: Primary assignment content is TextGenEd (see repo-textgened). Also home to Inoue's Labor-Based Grading Contracts (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0), whose appendices are catalogued as grading contract and labor-log records.

name: First-Year Composition Archive (FYCA)
content_scope: Contributed first-year writing syllabi, assignments, and course materials, searchable by title, description, institution, course name, course theme, contributor, year first taught, required/gen-ed status, and institution type.
default_license: All rights reserved (free access); Ethical Use Statement permits educational and scholarly use with attribution
api_notes: ColdFusion site; 'Show All' and search are POST forms to /discover/index.cfm (fields: searchtype=3 for show all, dbtable=syllabi|assignments|materials, SortOption).
notes: Published by the WAC Clearinghouse. Copyright stays with contributors; the Ethical Use Statement asks for attribution, bars commercial or political exploitation without authorization, and treats misrepresenting alterations as unethical. Link-only for the builder. 24 items (9 syllabi, 15 assignments) catalogued with ids prefixed 'fyca-'; the 'Show All' result pages returned 25 syllabi and 25 assignments, so later pages were not reviewed. Includes three Justin Lewis ENG302 (WWU, 2019) technical writing assignments.

name: Composition Studies: Course Designs
content_scope: Course Designs section of Composition Studies: a syllabus plus a critical reflection on the course's rationale. Back issues 1972-2015 are free as full-issue PDFs from the archive; issue pages for 2016-2025 give TOCs and 'some open access content'; recent issues are subscription.
default_license: All rights reserved (free access for older issues)
api_notes: Archive page https://compstudiesjournal.com/archive/ links full-issue PDFs (e.g., https://compstudiesjournal.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/43.1-full-issue.pdf). Course Designs are not linked individually; they must be located inside full-issue PDFs.
notes: No license statement on the site. Access note: the site says the archive offers full text for issues published seven years prior to the present. Course Designs are not separately addressable, so 14 Course Designs from 2011-2015 issues (39.1-43.2) were catalogued from issue tables of contents with the full-issue PDF as file_url and the start page in notes (ids prefixed 'compstudies-'). Usually 1-2 Course Designs per issue.

name: Xchanges: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Technical Communication, Rhetoric, and Writing Across the Curriculum
content_scope: Undergraduate (fall) and graduate (spring) student research in technical communication, writing/rhetoric, and WAC, including multimodal webtexts. Not an assignment journal; useful as student model texts.
default_license: Not stated on home page
api_notes: Issues at https://xchanges.org/archives/.
notes: Published by the UNM English Department. Examined because it was on the source list; it does not publish assignments or course designs, so no item records were made.

name: Kairos PraxisWiki
content_scope: Kairos section publishing short webtexts on digital writing pedagogy ('pedagogy in action'), several of which document classroom assignments (multimodal annotated bibliography, Twitter bots, social media rhetorical analysis, multimodal advocacy, remix assessment, digital badges).
default_license: All rights reserved (free access); no license statement found
api_notes: TikiWiki pages at tiki-index.php?page=...; still active (Issue 30.2, Jan 2026), rolling submissions.
notes: Not archived; active. Four assignment-focused webtexts catalogued as link-only (ids prefixed 'kairos-praxiswiki-').

name: Wiki Education (Wikipedia Student Program)
content_scope: Support for Wikipedia writing assignments: Dashboard assignment plans and trainings, instructor and student brochures, an example grading rubric, a knowledge-equity curriculum guide, a Theories handbook, and subject-specific editing handouts (science communication, linguistics, history, sociology, etc.).
default_license: CC BY-SA (site text 'All text CC-BY-SA except where noted'); Commons PDFs are CC BY-SA 3.0 or 4.0
api_notes: Handouts are hosted on Wikimedia Commons (category 'Wiki Education Foundation handouts'), which has the MediaWiki API. Dashboard (dashboard.wikiedu.org) hosts trainings and assignment design for enrolled US/Canadian courses; program enrollment is free but requires application.
notes: Seven items catalogued (ids prefixed 'wikiedu-'). Kairos 29.1 DiCaglio et al. note Wiki Ed materials target advanced editing and may need introductory supplements.

name: Association of Teachers of Technical Writing (ATTW)
content_scope: Professional organization site: TCQ journal, ATTW Book Series, blog, and public bibliographies (Contributions of Black Scholars in TPC; Works by BIPOC in TPC, as Google Docs).
default_license: Not stated
api_notes: No teaching-resource or syllabus repository linked from the home page; https://attw.org/resources/ returned 404 (Oct 2026).
notes: No openly licensed assignments or syllabi found. The BIPOC bibliographies are free and useful for building tech comm reading lists.

name: Council for Programs in Technical and Scientific Communication (CPTSC)
content_scope: Program-level resources: white papers, program review, conference proceedings (1974-2025), webinar resources, research grants, and the journal Programmatic Perspectives.
default_license: Not stated
api_notes: Programmatic Perspectives runs on OJS (https://programmaticperspectives.cptsc.org/index.php/jpp/index), so OAI-PMH is likely but was not checked.
notes: No syllabus bank or assignment collection found on the public site.

name: CCCC / NCTE resources
content_scope: Position statements, OWI state-of-the-art reports, Strategic Action Task Force resources, Writing Majors at a Glance (2015), and the MLA-CCCC Joint Task Force on Writing and AI (aiandwriting.hcommons.org).
default_license: Not stated
api_notes: aiandwriting.hcommons.org returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch.
notes: No free sample-syllabus bank found on the CCCC resources page. Position statements (e.g., on writing assessment, disability) are free to read and may pair with pedagogy units.

name: Open Syllabus
content_scope: Non-profit archive of syllabus metadata: 'Mapping the college curriculum across 32.9 million syllabi.' Tools: Analytics (what is assigned, by field and school), Galaxy (co-assignment map), Course Matcher.
default_license: Not openly licensed; anonymized metadata licensed to researchers on request and commercially; original documents not licensed
api_notes: No public API documented on the pages reviewed. Free Analytics account caps data at 2019 and hides syllabi; 30-day trial gives full access; organizational subscriptions only. Terms: 'portions of its syllabus metadata available to researchers for purposes of benefit to the public' and 'limited to portions of anonymized data'; specialized research requests by contact.
notes: Use as a signal for which readings writing courses actually assign (e.g., to rank OA readings), not as a source of reusable syllabi. Galaxy: https://galaxy.opensyllabus.org/; Analytics: https://analytics.opensyllabus.org/.

name: Digital.gov usability and user research guides
content_scope: U.S. GSA guides usable as UX assignment scaffolds: usability test script, interview script and debrief, interview checklist, research plan outline, participant agreements; links to Section508.gov sample personas for users with disabilities and the DHS Usability Testing Kit.
default_license: Public domain (U.S. government work); site policy: 'Most material on Digital.gov is free of copyright'
item_count_estimate: 7 guides on the usability topic page
api_notes: usability.gov now redirects (301) to digital.gov/topics/usability/. 18F Methods (methods.18f.gov, guides.18f.gov) no longer resolve (DNS failure, Oct 2026).
notes: Not classroom assignments; recorded as public-domain templates for usability testing and user research units. Three items catalogued (ids prefixed 'digitalgov-').

name: KC Works (Knowledge Commons repository; formerly Humanities Commons CORE, hcommons.org/deposits)
content_scope: General open repository for humanities and social science scholarship (about 46,500 records in October 2026). Its 'Instructional resource' type held 1,131 records: 540 syllabi, 516 'other' (assignment sheets, handouts, activities), 22 curricula, and 6 lesson plans. Writing-relevant material includes first-year writing syllabi, many multimodal and digital-writing assignments, and writing handouts. A large share comes from MLA's Digital Pedagogy in the Humanities curated collection (2020 deposits, mostly CC BY-NC).
default_license: No single default; each depositor picks a license. Most instructional records are Creative Commons (CC BY, CC BY-SA, CC BY-NC, CC BY-NC-SA, a few CC BY-NC-ND). Some are All Rights Reserved, a few legacy records show 0BSD, and some 2025-26 deposits have no license in metadata.
item_count_estimate: 1,131 instructional resources (540 syllabi); about 46,500 records in total
api_notes: InvenioRDM REST API, no key needed for public records. Search: GET https://works.hcommons.org/api/records?q=<query>&size=100&page=N (size=100 worked). Filter by type with the facet param resource_type=instructionalResource (subtypes instructionalResource-syllabus, -other, -curriculum, -lessonPlan). License is in metadata.rights[].id (e.g. cc-by-nc-sa-4.0) with a title and legalcode URL. Landing page: https://works.hcommons.org/records/{id}. File listing: /api/records/{id}/files. File content: /api/records/{id}/files/{key}/content. Elasticsearch field queries work, e.g. q=metadata.title:syllabus AND writing. Responses were slow (often 30-90 s per call). HEAD requests from curl to landing and file URLs returned 403 from the AWS load balancer, while GET calls to the JSON API worked. OAI-PMH was not tested.
notes: Best way to harvest: page through every resource_type=instructionalResource record (12 calls at size 100) and filter locally. Keyword search on its own ranks many journal articles above teaching materials. Technical, business, and science writing are thin; most of what exists comes from the Digital Pedagogy in the Humanities artifacts and a few single handouts. Some syllabi are deposited twice (e.g. the Trettien multimodal composition syllabus).

name: OER Commons (ISKME)
content_scope: General OER repository. Relevant holdings under subject 'Composition and Rhetoric' and material types Full Course, Syllabus, Module, Homework/Assignment, Lesson Plan. Searches this session: 'technical writing' full courses (46 results), Composition and Rhetoric full courses (50), syllabi (29), modules (72), 'writing assignment' homework/assignments (51), 'english composition' full courses (62).
default_license: Varies by item (each record states a CC license or other rights)
item_count_estimate: Hundreds of composition/technical/business writing items; about 50-70 per material-type filter within Composition and Rhetoric
api_notes: No public API endpoint found (/api and /oer-api return 404). robots.txt disallows /search, /courses/*, and /api/* (crawl-delay 1), so bulk scraping of search and course records is not permitted; courseware/lesson pages are not disallowed. Plain requests without browser-like headers get 403.
notes: Hubs relevant to writing courses: Open Washington (/hubs/open-washington; Open Course Library), OERizona (/hubs/oerizona), California Community Colleges Hub (/hubs/ccc), Open Massachusetts (/hubs/masscc), Oregon State University (/hubs/OregonState), Information Literacy (/hubs/infolit), Missouri, Nebraska, Open Illinois, SC Technical College System, UNC System, Michigan Community College Association. Many items are Oregon WR 121/122/227 syllabi, Open Course Library packages, MIT OCW courses, and Tennessee Board of Regents and California ROTEL/OFAR grant products. Item metadata quality varies (e.g., WR 227 tagged as Mathematics). Year is usually only available as 'Date Added'.

name: MERLOT (Multimedia Educational Resource for Learning and Online Teaching)
content_scope: Peer-reviewed referatory of links to learning materials from the California State University system and partners. Discipline Humanities/English/Language/Composition and Rhetoric (category=343301): 10 items typed 'Assignment' and 172 typed 'Online Course' this session; keyword 'technical writing assignment' gave 31 hits, mostly K-12 lesson plans.
default_license: Varies by item; each record has a 'Creative Commons' field (a specific CC license, 'No', or 'Unknown'). Many writing items are 'No' or 'Unknown'.
item_count_estimate: About 180 Composition and Rhetoric assignments/online courses; few true writing-course assignment prompts
api_notes: MERLOT web services reportedly require a license key (per task brief); the API documentation was not reachable this session. Search pages (materials.htm?category=...&materialType=...) render server-side and parse cleanly. An RSS endpoint (materials.rss) exists but returned generic items and ignored the keyword parameter. The external 'Go to Material' URL is behind a POST form (/merlot/gom.htm with CSRF token), so source URLs cannot be scraped from detail pages without the API.
notes: Holds Washington Open Course Library courses (ENGL 101, ENGL 102, Technical Writing), Lumen/NOVA zELI College Composition I (CC BY-NC 4.0), CMU OLI Argument Diagramming, McMurrey's Online Technical Writing (CC BY 4.0, filed as Reference Material), and scattered instructor-submitted prompts. Much of the Assignment material type in this discipline is K-12 or developmental.

name: CUNY Academic Works: Open Educational Resources series (per-campus collections)
content_scope: Faculty-deposited OER syllabi, assignments and course materials from CUNY campuses, in per-campus series such as cc_oers (City College), ny_oers (City Tech), lg_oers (LaGuardia), kb_oers (Kingsborough), bm_oers (BMCC), si_oers (Staten Island), gc_oers (Graduate Center). Strong on FYC/FIQWS, Writing for the Sciences/Engineering/Social Sciences/Humanities (WAC tier), and some business communication.
default_license: Varies by item; each record states a CC license (mostly CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, CC BY-NC 4.0 or CC BY 4.0).
item_count_estimate: cc_oers alone lists about 540 items; browse pages fetched this session for 12 campus series listed at least 1,600 items across all disciplines (some series may have more pages than were fetched)
api_notes:
bepress Digital Commons. Browse pages at //index.html, index.2.html, etc. list items as

; each record has license text and a viewcontent.cgi PDF link. bepress sites usually expose OAI-PMH at /do/oai/ but this was not tested.
notes: Licenses verified on individual records, not as a site-wide default. Some campus series (bb_oers, qc_oers, hc_oers, ol_oers, me_oers) returned no listings under the URL pattern used. Not one of the excluded repositories.

name: MIT OpenCourseWare
content_scope: Full course sites (syllabus, calendar, assignments, readings) for MIT courses, including Comparative Media Studies/Writing (21W: science writing, rhetoric, tech comm, graduate technical writing), English Language Studies (21G: writing for multilingual scientists and engineers), and Sloan management communication (15.279, 15.280, 15.281, 15.289).
default_license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (site footer link on course pages); older archived courses on MIT DSpace use CC BY-NC-SA 3.0
item_count_estimate: about 40 writing/communication courses identified in the sitemap; 2,500+ courses overall
api_notes: https://ocw.mit.edu/sitemap.xml is a sitemap index with one sitemap per course; course syllabus pages follow /courses/<slug>/pages/syllabus/. Full course zips downloadable per course. Some syllabus pages caused redirect loops for the fetcher; course home pages worked.
notes: Several retired courses (e.g., 21W.732 Intro to Tech Communication) live only on MIT DSpace.

name: GALILEO Open Learning Materials (Affordable Learning Georgia)
content_scope: University System of Georgia OER repository: open textbooks, ancillary materials (open courses), and Grants Collections that bundle a syllabus, proposal and final report for each Textbook Transformation Grant. English, Communication (incl. Technical Communication) and Business subject areas each have ancillary, grants and textbook series.
default_license: Varies by item; records checked this session were CC BY 4.0 (one CC BY-SA 3.0).
item_count_estimate: english-collections 11, english-ancillary 7, communication-collections 5, communication-ancillary 8; all-ancillary runs 3 browse pages (about 100 per page)
api_notes: bepress Digital Commons; subject series at /<subject>-collections, /<subject>-ancillary, /<subject>-textbooks. Browse by license at /license/. Syllabus files are viewcontent.cgi attachments (filename=N&type=additional). Many open courses are hosted on alg.manifoldapp.org.
notes: Grants Collections are a reliable source of CC BY syllabi tied to named open textbooks.

name: City Tech OpenLab (CUNY)
content_scope: WordPress course, project and OER sites at New York City College of Technology, including ENG 1101 and ENG 2575 Technical Writing course sites and the 'In Conversation' ENG 1101 OER reader.
default_license: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike (site footer; home page links CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, some course sites state 4.0)
api_notes: Course directory at https://openlab.citytech.cuny.edu/courses (not inspected). Individual WordPress sites may expose /feed/ RSS.
notes: Footer license is site-wide; individual sites sometimes add their own statement. Site reports 46,000 members.

name: Google for Developers: Technical Writing Courses
content_scope: Four short technical writing courses for engineers: Technical Writing One, Technical Writing Two, Tech Writing for Accessibility, Writing Helpful Error Messages, with pre-class lessons and facilitator guides for instructor-led sessions.
default_license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 License (code samples Apache 2.0), except as otherwise noted
notes: Facilitator materials listed under 'For Facilitators'. Technical Writing Two includes a unit on using LLMs in tech writing.

name: Lumen Learning open courseware (Candela)
content_scope: Open courseware built on Pressbooks/Candela, some with instructor-resource sections that include a sample syllabus (e.g., SUNY Technical Writing).
default_license: Varies by page; each page carries a 'Licenses and Attributions' block (the tech writing sample syllabus page is CC BY-SA).
api_notes: Instructor-resource sections are labeled log-in required, though some pages render publicly.
notes: The public Lumen catalog page lists only English Composition I and Developmental Writing in this area.

name: Syllabus (peer-reviewed journal of syllabi)
content_scope: Formerly published peer-reviewed course syllabi, essays and 'tool box' entries.
notes: As of 2026-10-17 syllabusjournal.org returns a 301 redirect to an unrelated domain (sodamountain.com), so the journal appears defunct at this address. License could not be checked. Back issues may survive in the Internet Archive (not checked).
